scope: All 34 original bibliography entries and their cited claims in the main paper, appendix and related-work comparison table. One direct documentation citation was added.
method: Checked primary arXiv records, proceedings/publisher pages or paper PDFs, author repositories and exact official model cards. Title, author prefix/order, year, venue and URL-to-work identity were compared. Cited passages were checked for claim support; this is not validation of ResolveAI experiment scores. Official indexed proceedings records were cross-checked with an independent primary source when direct page retrieval returned a browser challenge or HTTP 403.
important_resolutions: MMPerspective official HTML differs from its paper PDF in the first author name and author order. Preserve the published PDF author list; no manuscript author correction is justified.
VisualToolBench retains its verifiable 2025 arXiv citation. A possible ICLR 2026 workshop publication is not promoted to a main-conference acceptance or treated as independently confirmed here.
MissingBench remains a preprint; submission to a workshop is not acceptance.
SmolVLM2 now cites the paper explicitly recommended by the exact official model card. Qwen3.5-9B retains its genuine official model-card reference.
OpenAI Models and Decisions are separate real documentation resources; the earlier composite reference title was replaced with their actual titles.

claim_support.summary: The ACL abstract explicitly restricts the perceptual field and requires active zooming or shifting, directly supporting both manuscript descriptions.

The official abstract states that image-text claims have question-answer annotations containing web evidence and that annotation uses a two-stage sufficiency check. This directly supports the main description and the appendix table's annotated web evidence and sufficiency checks. These are annotation-quality checks, not a claim that AVerImaTeC uses ResolveAI's paired access conditions.

The paper explicitly includes visual correspondence and multi-view reasoning, supporting the main descriptions. The appendix comparison table's visual-perception target is also supported. Section 3.1 describes repurposing existing vision datasets, and Sections 3.2/4.3 describe constructed visual prompts/alternatives and prompt variations; these support image reuse and controlled visual variants as prior practices. The paper does not establish ResolveAI's own evidence-access construction, which is the authors' separately stated contribution.
